facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: GFL's financial base at September 30, 2026 is a larger, more levered consolidated group than at year-end 2025, and the leverage figure depends entirely on which EBITDA and debt definition is used. Reported debt before deferred costs rose by 4,269.7 to 11,696.4 while cash rose by 210.9 to 296.5; the increase coincides with 2,569.8 of nine-month acquisition spend, the SECURE share-and-cash purchase that closed September 1, 2026, and a Term Loan B Facility entered on August 28, 2026; the sources do not bridge the debt movement line by line. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,257.1 captures SECURE for one month only, so total debt over that EBITDA is 5.18x and net 5.05x, whereas management's Net Leverage of 3.8x adds 730.9 of run-rate adjustments to reach 2,988.0. The revolver covenant is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and management states compliance; the agreement definition is not in the pack, so headroom is not calculable here and the unadjusted 5.18x must not be read as a breach. Cash conversion improved at the management-defined Adjusted Free Cash Flow level (484.9 for nine months 2026 against 331.3), but operating cash flow is stated after 193.1 of working-capital outflow and the earnings measure adds back 172.1 of cash costs. All FY2025 figures other than the year-end balance sheet comparatives and management's trailing-twelve-month figures are unavailable, and the year-end 2025 balance sheet was revised after Q1.

facts.label: Liquidity and covenants
facts.text: - Facilities. GFL has access to a $2,000.0 million revolving credit facility (available in Canadian and US dollars), a $25.0 million revolving credit facility (available in US dollars) and an aggregate $1,000.0 million accordion feature (Q3FS page:12), maturing April 29, 2030, so neither the revolver nor the Term Loan B Facility expires within twelve months (the EDC facility term is not stated). The EDC Guaranteed LC Facility gives $250.0 million of letters of credit that are 100% guaranteed by Export Development Canada (Q3FS page:18) against 187.8 used. - Availability. The sources print commitments, drawings and letters of credit but no statement of the amount available. The derived revolver availability range is 809.7 to 1,157.0 at September 30, 2026 (Calculations). Cash is 296.5. The subsidiary facilities (a US$30.0 million revolver undrawn and a US$100.0 million revolver with US$43.0 million drawn) are USD and outside the parent's revolver; they are not added. - Covenants. The Revolving Credit Agreement contains a Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA and an Interest Coverage Ratio (each as defined in the Revolving Credit Agreement) financial maintenance covenant. (Q3FS page:12). The leverage test is equal to or less than 5.00 to 1.00 for a period of four complete fiscal quarters following completion of a Material Acquisition (Q3FS page:13) and otherwise 4.50 to 1.00; the interest coverage test is at least 3.00 to 1.00; GFL was in compliance with these covenants. (Q3FS page:13). No step-down date is printed. The reported covenant figures are not printed, so headroom is Not calculable. The metric computed here differs from the covenant: it uses unadjusted trailing Adjusted EBITDA, debt before deferred costs and cash netting, while the agreement defines Total Net Funded Debt and Adjusted EBITDA itself, and the release says Run-Rate EBITDA is calculated in accordance with the terms of our revolving credit agreement (Q3PR page:10).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: GFL is a diversified solid waste and industrial waste processing business in Canada and the United States whose 2026 credit story is acquisition-driven. In the third quarter of 2026 acquisitions contributed 18.7% of the 27.2% revenue growth, organic growth was 7.4% of which price was 5.7% and volume was negative, so the operating model currently relies on price realisation and acquired scale rather than volume. The SECURE acquisition (completed September 1, 2026, total consideration approximately 5,414.1, funded with 4,334.8 of shares and 1,079.3 of cash) is the transaction that changes the credit: it raised Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangible assets from 1,942.0 to 6,902.2, added Western Canada industrial waste processing, disposal and recycling, and brought new crude oil transportation and storage commitments that did not exist at year-end 2025. The accounting is provisional, and the debt financing is documented in the CP-1 handoff rather than by transaction-level sources, so use of proceeds is partly inferred. There is no sponsor named in the sources, the controlling shareholder position is not described, and the board has formed a Special Committee to review unsolicited proposals to take the company private; the outcome is after the cutoff and no terms are supplied. Governance evidence is mixed: documented actions include a large 2025 share repurchase and a cash payment to the Founder and CEO in place of share-unit settlement, offset by an independent committee process. Business description, customer concentration, contract tenor and control rights are Insufficient Information because the annual information form is not in the pack.

facts.text: The principal transaction is the acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. A definitive agreement was entered on April 12, 2026 (On April 12, 2026, GFL entered into a definitive agreement pursuant to which it has agreed to acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. Management said SECURE shareholders approved it in May (SECURE shareholders approved the transaction in May (Q2PR page:1), Management Language), and it closed on September 1, 2026 for total consideration of approximately 5,414.1, of which 4,334.8 was shares and 1,079.3 cash, with 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares issued in the nine months (Q3FS page:6 and page:16). SECURE is described as an operator of waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling located in Western Canada and North Dakota (Q3FS page:7). The purchase price allocation is provisional: goodwill recognized for SECURE is 4,968.1, property and equipment 1,616.9, other long-term liabilities 1,006.6 and closure obligations 271.8 (Q3FS page:6), and adjustments may significantly impact the recognized values of intangible assets, goodwill, property and equipment and deferred income tax liabilities (Q3FS page:7). SECURE net working capital includes cash of 73.4. No source identifies a sponsor. A SECURE nominee joins the board, which grows to nine directors (Q3PR page:2). The status is completed, with provisional accounting.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: GFL is a scaled, price-led North American waste operator whose credit has become more leveraged, and the fundamental view is cautious but not adverse. The strongest support is recurring collection revenue and a Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% with no named maturity until 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt is 5.18x trailing Adjusted EBITDA on an unadjusted basis against management's 3.8x run-rate figure, which relies on CAD 730.9 million of management adjustments. The outcome is decided by whether SECURE earnings and synergies arrive, how the revolver covenant defines its debt and EBITDA, and what the open take-private review brings.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: GFL is a scaled, price-led North American waste operator whose credit has become more leveraged, and the fundamental view is cautious but not adverse. The strongest support is recurring collection revenue and a Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% with no named maturity until 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt is 5.18x trailing Adjusted EBITDA on an unadjusted basis against management's 3.8x run-rate figure, which relies on CAD 730.9 million of management adjustments. The outcome is decided by whether SECURE earnings and synergies arrive, how the revolver covenant defines its debt and EBITDA, and what the open take-private review brings.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Debt has stepped up faster than earnings, and the leverage reading depends on the definition. GFL carried CAD 11,696.4 million of debt before deferred costs at September 30, 2026, up from CAD 7,426.7 million at year-end 2025 [CP-1 financial table], while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is CAD 2,257.1 million and includes SECURE for only the month after its September 1, 2026 closing [CP-1 chart data: leverage]. Unadjusted, that is 5.18x total and 5.05x net; management's run-rate basis adds CAD 730.9 million to reach 3.8x [CP-1]. The revolver test is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and management states compliance, but the agreement's own definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable and the unadjusted figure should not be read as a breach [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]. This is Analyst Interpretation resting on Documentary Fact figures.

citations.quote: Debt has stepped up faster than earnings, and the leverage reading depends on the definition. GFL carried CAD 11,696.4 million of debt before deferred costs at September 30, 2026, up from CAD 7,426.7 million at year-end 2025 [CP-1 financial table], while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is CAD 2,257.1 million and includes SECURE for only the month after its September 1, 2026 closing [CP-1 chart data: leverage]. Unadjusted, that is 5.18x total and 5.05x net; management's run-rate basis adds CAD 730.9 million to reach 3.8x [CP-1]. The revolver test is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and management states compliance, but the agreement's own definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable and the unadjusted figure should not be read as a breach [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]. This is Analyst Interpretation resting on Documentary Fact figures.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Operating performance is solid but growth is bought and priced rather than volume-led. In Q3 2026 revenue rose 27.2%, of which acquisitions were 18.7% and organic 7.4%, with price 5.7% and volume (0.1)% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 678.7 million, up from CAD 535.1 million, at a 31.5% margin against 31.6% a year earlier, while the USA segment margin fell 2.3 points and Canada rose 2.1 points. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months 2026 against income of CAD 123.5 million, driven by CAD 482.9 million of interest and other finance costs and non-cash foreign exchange and fair-value charges, so earnings quality rests on the management measure [CP-1].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, recurring route-based revenue: collection is 60.9% of gross revenue for nine months 2026, which gives revenue visibility even though contract terms are not supplied (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact rows [CP-1A company and operating model]). Second, pricing power in the reported numbers: Q3 2026 price of 5.7% and surcharges of 1.5% drove organic growth of 7.4%, and the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.4% against 29.9% (Documentary Fact [CP-1A; CP-1]). Third, funding diversification and a staggered profile: a revolver to April 2030, a Term Loan B Facility to August 2033 and eight series of notes with maturities from 2028 to 2034, with no named instrument due before 2028 (Documentary Fact [CP-1 debt instruments]). Fourth, cash conversion improved on the management measure, with Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million against CAD 331.3 million (Management Language [CP-1]). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated by the issuer at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact, issuer assertion [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]). Sixth, an independent committee process governs the take-private review (Documentary Fact [CP-1A ownership, governance and behaviour]).

spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for GFL Environmental Inc. (issuer id gfl; Ontario-incorporated registrant, NYSE and TSX ticker GFL; sector Refuse Systems; country Canada), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, reporting currency CAD (context file, run block). Requested downstream consumers: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. Question answered here: can the supplied source set support those four consumers, and what remains blocked or limited. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures beyond the tie-outs shown in Calculations. Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY.

Scope notes. The perimeter is GFL Environmental Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries (`all references to “GFL”, “we”, “our”, “us”, “the Company” or similar terms refer to GFL Environmental Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries` (40F page:2)). The context names no borrower, parent, guarantor or sponsor and holds no deal terms, quotes, ratings, peers or research questions; blank context values are treated as unknown, not zero. No source is dated after the cutoff 2026-11-05. Figures in the interim sources are CAD millions unless stated (`The Interim Financial Statements are presented in Canadian dollars which is GFL’s functional currency.` (Q3FS page:5)), and the Q3 release says `All references to “$” in this press release are to Canadian dollars, unless otherwise noted.` (Q3PR page:10). Several debt lines are USD instruments carried in CAD.
## Sources
Issuer sources relied on (name and sha256 as supplied by CP-OS). Short keys in brackets are used for locators below; a page is the retained chunk `page:N`, not a printed page.

Run context (settings and inputs, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 8fcb7a42287c8f6efb39cea12a8c3d3db65bfbc11e1653a358aafe84da574912.
Supplied handoffs: none. CP-0 is the first module in this run and CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff.
Ignored by the launcher: `_retrieval.json` (retrieval metadata, not a source).
### Source profiles

Document family, authority, perimeter, period and version relationships come from located content, not file names. Where a file name carries a date that the text does not repeat, it is treated as a label only.
| Key | Document family and authority | Entity and perimeter | Period and basis | Version relationships |

| 40F | Annual report cover on Form 40-F, signed by the issuer. A filing wrapper only: it incorporates the annual information form, MD&A and audited statements by reference to separate exhibits that are not in the pack. | GFL Environmental Inc., registrant; consolidated | `For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025` (40F page:1) | Superseded in detail by later interim statements; its exhibits are absent, so it controls only cover, share-count and exhibit-list facts. |

| Q1FS | Unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements with notes (IFRS, filed as 6-K exhibit): controlling for Q1 statement and note facts. | GFL consolidated | `For the three months ended March 31, 2026` (Q1FS page:1) | Separate active source. Shows the 2025 year-end equity-method investment before revision. |

| Q1PR | Earnings release with non-IFRS reconciliations and guidance: attributed management claims, not controlling over the statements. | GFL consolidated | Q1 2026, dated April 29, 2026 in its text | Separate active source. |

| Q2FS | Unaudited interim statements with notes for three and six months to June 30, 2026. | GFL consolidated | `For the three and six months ended June 30, 2026` (Q2FS page:1) | Separate active source. First source to show the revised 2025 year-end comparatives. |
| Q2PR | Earnings release for Q2 2026, dated July 29, 2026 in its text. | GFL consolidated | Q2 2026 | Separate active source. |

| Q3PR | Earnings release for Q3 2026, dated October 28, 2026 in its text: carries guidance, the Net Leverage table, the special-committee statement and non-IFRS reconciliations. | GFL consolidated | Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 | Overlaps Q3FS on the condensed statements; Q3FS is retained as the controlling source for IFRS facts, Q3PR for non-IFRS measures and management statements. |

| Q3FS | Unaudited interim statements with notes, including long-term debt, commitments, segments and share capital. Controlling source for current-period IFRS facts. | GFL consolidated; names no subsidiary guarantor group | `For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026` (Q3FS page:1); `The Board of Directors approved the Interim Financial Statements on October 28, 2026.` (Q3FS page:5) | Latest statements. Revises 2025 comparatives (see Findings). |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The pack supports a source-based credit snapshot for the latest quarter in Canadian dollars, with limitations. Interim statements, earnings releases and a debt note are retained; the annual report is only a cover document. | Medium | No audited full-year statements, annual MD&A, annual information form, credit agreement or indentures are in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The latest quarter is well covered: statements, debt note, covenant wording, commitments, segments and non-IFRS reconciliations are all retained. | Current balance sheet, cash flow and leverage inputs can be traced to located pages. | High |

| The annual report is a cover document; the full-year audited statements, annual MD&A and annual information form are not retained. | Full-year 2025 income and cash flow detail, contractual obligations and business description cannot be sourced beyond comparatives. | High |

| Debt terms are limited to the interim debt note; covenant levels are printed but the credit agreement is not. | Covenant headroom, guarantor structure and maturity profile need caution and cannot be fully tested. | Medium |

| A take-private review and a large acquisition completed in the third quarter are described, with provisional acquisition accounting. | Leverage and ownership could change; the review outcome is not in the sources. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four requested consumers. Coverage is strong for the latest quarter and the three quarters before it: five interim documents give statements, notes, segment data and non-IFRS reconciliations in CAD under IFRS, and the Q3 pair supplies the debt table, covenant wording, letters of credit, performance bonds and commodity commitments. The strongest contrary evidence is that the only annual document is a filing cover page whose exhibits are not retained, so FY2025 is available only as year-end balance sheet comparatives (which were revised after the first quarter) and as management's trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA for 2025. No legal financing document is supplied, so covenant definitions, guarantor groups, security packages and call terms rest on interim-note summaries. The next evidence action is to add the FY2025 annual report exhibits (audited statements, MD&A, annual information form) and the revolving credit agreement and note indentures if available; absent that, downstream modules must carry the limitations below and label every FY2025 figure as a comparative or trailing-twelve-month figure.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Status | Evidence available | Limitations carried forward |

| CP-1 (financial and credit data) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Q3 statements and notes, debt note with every instrument line, covenant levels, interest paid in cash, segment and Adjusted EBITDA tables, Net Leverage table | FY2025 income statement and cash flow not retained; USD principal not printed for most notes; no maturity table by year; revolver availability not stated; reported covenant ratio and headroom not printed |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Segment and service-line revenue, acquisition notes, SECURE acquisition accounting, special-committee statement, share capital, related-party note | Annual information form absent (business description, ownership and control, risk factors); SECURE agreement and any take-private proposal terms absent; acquisition accounting provisional |
| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Same as above; CP-OS sequences it after CP-1 and CP-1A | Inherits both sets of limitations; no ratings or market data in the context |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validator) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | All seven sources are text-extracted with page locators and can be quote-checked | Extraction status is not a fidelity review; tables were read from text, not images; no image or chart inspection claimed |
### Coverage, strongest evidence and perimeter

- Period coverage. Statements and notes exist for Q1 (three months), Q2 (three and six months) and Q3 (three and nine months) of 2026, each with comparative periods of 2025, so discrete quarters and quarter versus year-to-date distinctions are separable. FY2025 as a full period is covered only through management's trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA (`Trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA(2) 2,257.1 1,985.0` (Q3PR page:14)).

- Perimeter. All figures are consolidated GFL. Equity-method associates, including the retained stake in the divested environmental services business (`GFL has the option to repurchase the balance of the equity of GFL Environmental Services (the “Call Option”).` (Q3FS page:8)), sit outside Adjusted EBITDA by definition of the add-back. Non-wholly-owned subsidiaries carry stand-alone credit facilities inside long-term debt (`Certain of GFL’s non-wholly owned subsidiaries have stand alone credit facilities included in other in long-term debt.` (Q3FS page:13)). The issuer-versus-restricted-group distinction is not drawn in any source.

- Debt. The Q3 debt note lists the revolving credit facility, the Term Loan B Facility, eight series of USD notes (two of them secured at issue, one since released from collateral), the tax-exempt bonds and other facilities, and totals `Total long-term debt 11,671.4 7,422.6` (Q3FS page:11) in CAD millions for September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025. Maturities appear in the footnotes, not in a year-by-year table.

- Covenants. `equal to or less than 5.00 to 1.00 for a period of four complete fiscal quarters following completion of a Material Acquisition` (Q3FS page:13) applies to Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA, with `GFL was in compliance with these covenants.` (Q3FS page:13). The ratio as defined in the agreement is not printed.

- Off-balance-sheet and other claims. `letters of credit totaling approximately $535.1 million outstanding` (Q3FS page:18), `$187.8 million in outstanding letters of credit under the EDC Guaranteed LC Facility` (Q3FS page:18), `performance bonds totaling $2,324.1 million` (Q3FS page:19), `crude oil transportation commitments totaling $561.4 million` (Q3FS page:19), and lease obligations on the balance sheet (`Lease obligations 605.7 450.6` (Q3FS page:2) non-current). Pension and retiree medical obligations: no mention found in any source (searched "pension", "retirement", "post-employment").

- Management claims. Guidance, run-rate EBITDA, Net Leverage and Adjusted Free Cash Flow are management non-IFRS measures; guidance has no reconciliation (`GFL does not have information available to provide a quantitative reconciliation of such projections` (Q3PR page:3)). They are attributed claims, not controlling facts.
### Subsequent events and version relationships

- The Q3 release states a take-private review: `Special Committee of independent directors to review unsolicited inbound proposals to take the Company private` (Q3PR page:1) with `final deadline of November 9, 2026` (Q3PR page:1). The date falls after the cutoff 2026-11-05 and is a future term, not an outcome. No proposal terms, bidders or financing are in the sources.

- The Q3 statements carry no subsequent-events note (searched all seven sources for "subsequent"; only the Q1 statements have one, `Subsequent to March 31, 2026, GFL completed 5 acquisitions` (Q1FS page:15)). Events between September 30, 2026 and the cutoff are therefore evidenced only by the Q3 release dated October 28, 2026.

- Provisional accounting: `the initial purchase price allocation is provisional and subject to adjustment during the measurement period` (Q3FS page:7) for SECURE, acquired `On September 1, 2026, GFL acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of SECURE for total consideration of approximately $5,414.1 million.` (Q3FS page:7). Downstream goodwill, intangible and net debt analysis is therefore provisional.

- Revised comparatives: Q1 shows the year-end 2025 equity-method investment as `Investments accounted for using the equity method 3 1,865.4 1,898.0` (Q1FS page:1) while Q2 and Q3 show it as revised to 1,805.3 and explain `Investments accounted for using the equity method $ 1,898.0 $ (92.7 ) $ 1,805.3` (Q3FS page:9). The revision is described as not material by management. The Q3 comparatives control; the earlier quarters stay active as separate sources, and any use of Dec 2025 figures must name the version.
## Calculations

CP-0 performs no normalization. The items below are coverage counts and arithmetic tie-outs of printed figures that test whether the sources agree with each other; they are not new analytical figures. All amounts are CAD millions.
| Check | Inputs and locators | Result |
| Retained pages, all issuer sources | 5 + 15 + 16 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 20 (page counts of the seven retained sources, table in Sources) | 110 pages across 7 sources |

| Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA sums to nine months | Q1 478.5 (Q1PR page:2), Q2 591.2 (Q2PR page:1), Q3 678.7 (Q3PR page:2) | 478.5 + 591.2 + 678.7 = 1,748.4, equal to the nine-month figure printed in Q3PR page:2 |

Financial base view for GFL Environmental Inc. (issuer id gfl; consolidated group, parent-level registrant), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 (three months to September 30, 2026) against FY2025, reporting currency CAD (context file). All amounts are CAD millions under IFRS unless stated; USD instruments appear at their CAD carrying value, and the Q3 release states `All references to “$” in this press release are to Canadian dollars, unless otherwise noted.` (Q3PR page:10). Scope: extract and label the reported financial base (income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, debt, liquidity, covenants, claims outside debt, quality of the Adjusted EBITDA measure) and compute leverage, coverage and liquidity metrics from printed inputs only, with periods and perimeter labelled. No outside knowledge of the company is used and no source after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used as fact. The reporting perimeter is GFL Environmental Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries; no issuer-only, restricted-group or guarantor-only statements are in the pack, so none can be given. ## Findings
### Reader summary

On unadjusted trailing Adjusted EBITDA, leverage is above management's 3.8x run-rate figure and the 5.00x covenant level, so the covenant definition decides the headroom. | Medium | The credit agreement and full-year 2025 statements are not in the pack, so covenant headroom and full-year cash interest cannot be tested. |

| Total debt rose to 11,696.4 from 7,426.7 at year-end 2025 while trailing Adjusted EBITDA includes only one month of SECURE. | Unadjusted leverage is 5.18x against management's run-rate 3.8x; the gap rests on 730.9 of management adjustments. | High |
| Cash interest paid was 371.7 for nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of 1,748.4. | Coverage of 4.70x on that basis; the lumpy semi-annual coupons make single quarters unreliable. | Medium |

### Financial base view

GFL's financial base at September 30, 2026 is a larger, more levered consolidated group than at year-end 2025, and the leverage figure depends entirely on which EBITDA and debt definition is used. Reported debt before deferred costs rose by 4,269.7 to 11,696.4 while cash rose by 210.9 to 296.5; the increase coincides with 2,569.8 of nine-month acquisition spend, the SECURE share-and-cash purchase that closed September 1, 2026, and a Term Loan B Facility entered on August 28, 2026; the sources do not bridge the debt movement line by line. Trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,257.1 captures SECURE for one month only, so total debt over that EBITDA is 5.18x and net 5.05x, whereas management's Net Leverage of 3.8x adds 730.9 of run-rate adjustments to reach 2,988.0. The revolver covenant is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and management states compliance; the agreement definition is not in the pack, so headroom is not calculable here and the unadjusted 5.18x must not be read as a breach. Cash conversion improved at the management-defined Adjusted Free Cash Flow level (484.9 for nine months 2026 against 331.3), but operating cash flow is stated after 193.1 of working-capital outflow and the earnings measure adds back 172.1 of cash costs. All FY2025 figures other than the year-end balance sheet comparatives and management's trailing-twelve-month figures are unavailable, and the year-end 2025 balance sheet was revised after Q1.

No step-down date is printed. The reported covenant figures are not printed, so headroom is Not calculable. The metric computed here differs from the covenant: it uses unadjusted trailing Adjusted EBITDA, debt before deferred costs and cash netting, while the agreement defines Total Net Funded Debt and Adjusted EBITDA itself, and the release says Run-Rate EBITDA is `calculated in accordance with the terms of our revolving credit agreement` (Q3PR page:10).
### Earnings quality and cash flow

- Add-backs. Nine months 2026 EBITDA of 1,203.4 becomes Adjusted EBITDA of 1,748.4 after 545.0 of add-backs (Q3PR page:15; Calculations). Of these, 172.1 are cash costs: transaction costs 70.6, acquisition, rebranding and integration costs 27.3 and Founder/CEO remuneration 74.2, which is `cash payment to the Founder and CEO, which payment had been previously satisfied through the issuance of restricted share units` (Q3FS page:16). Share-based payments of 87.0, foreign exchange and derivative losses of 192.6 and the Call Option charge of 45.0 are non-cash.

- Cash conversion. Operating cash flow of 950.1 for nine months 2026 is after 193.1 of working-capital outflow (Q3FS page:4) and 371.7 of cash interest. Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 adds back, among other items, 104.5 of cash transaction costs, 27.3 integration costs, 74.2 CEO remuneration and 182.4 of incremental growth investments (Q3PR page:18); management describes conversion as `improving Adjusted Free Cash Flow1 conversion toward the mid 40% range` (Q3PR page:1).

- Net loss drivers. Net loss from continuing operations of 409.8 for nine months 2026 follows interest and other finance costs of 482.9, a loss on foreign exchange of 196.7, a Call Option fair value charge of 45.0 and an equity-method loss of 48.0.
### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

- Financing. The Term Loan B Facility was entered on August 28, 2026 and matures August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%; the revolver was amended and restated through September 1, 2026; the 5.500% 2034 Notes and 5.625% 2031 Notes are on the June 30, 2026 balance sheet (1,421.0 and 1,065.8, Q2FS page:10). Cross-currency interest rate swaps were entered on the 5.625% 2031 Notes on June 25, 2026 (fixing 4.480%) and on the Term Loan B Facility on August 28, 2026 (fixing 5.009%) (Q3FS page:18). Q3 2026 debt issued was 2,438.9 and repaid 1,320.3.

- SECURE. `On September 1, 2026, GFL acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of SECURE for total consideration of approximately $5,414.1 million.` (Q3FS page:7): shares 4,334.8 and cash 1,079.3. Goodwill recognized was 4,968.1. The allocation is provisional. GFL also acquired 13 other businesses in nine months, each individually immaterial; total net assets acquired in nine months were 7,012.6 including SECURE, of which others 1,598.5.

- Guidance (management, not a fact). Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA approximately 2,490 to 2,495, Adjusted Free Cash Flow approximately 1,020, cash interest approximately 455 and `Net Leverage2 is estimated to be in the mid 3s by the end of 2026` (Q3PR page:3). Guidance excludes acquisitions not yet completed.

- After quarter end. The Q3 statements contain no subsequent-events note. The release dated October 28, 2026 records a Special Committee reviewing take-private proposals with a deadline of November 9, 2026 for updated proposals, a date after the cutoff (Q3PR page:1). No proposal terms are supplied.

- Revised comparatives. The December 31, 2025 equity-method investment was 1,898.0 as first reported and 1,805.3 as revised (Q3FS page:9); this figure and the 2025 comparatives in this handoff are the revised ones, as in the Q3 statements.
## Calculations
All amounts are CAD millions. Inputs are the cited printed figures; results are computed here and rounded to two decimals for ratios.
| Calculation | Formula and inputs | Result |
| Total debt / trailing Adjusted EBITDA, Sep 30, 2026 | 11,696.4 (Q3FS page:11) / 2,257.1 (Q3PR page:14) | 5.18x |
| Net debt, Sep 30, 2026 | 11,696.4 - 296.5 | 11,399.9 (equal to the figure printed in Q3PR page:14) |
| Net debt / trailing Adjusted EBITDA, Sep 30, 2026 | 11,399.9 / 2,257.1 | 5.05x |

| Total debt plus leases / trailing Adjusted EBITDA, Sep 30, 2026 | (11,696.4 + 705.0) / 2,257.1 where leases = 99.3 + 605.7 | 5.49x; at Dec 31, 2025 (7,426.7 + 510.5) / 1,985.0 = 4.00x, leases 59.9 + 450.6 |
| Change in debt | 11,696.4 - 7,426.7 | 4,269.7 increase |
| Nine months 2025 ex early-termination interest (illustrative) | 1,476.3 / (371.1 - 68.9 = 302.2) | 4.89x; not used in the chart because the 68.9 is management-reported on a different basis |

| Revolver availability, Sep 30, 2026 | Commitments 2,000.0 + 25.0 = 2,025.0; less drawn 868.0 = 1,157.0; less non-EDC letters of credit (535.1 - 187.8 = 347.3) = 809.7 | 809.7 to 1,157.0; the lower figure assumes every letter of credit outside the EDC facility sits on the revolver, which the note does not say |

| Cash costs added back, nine months 2026 | 70.6 + 27.3 + 74.2 | 172.1, which is 9.84% of Adjusted EBITDA of 1,748.4; Q3 2026 transaction costs 46.5 plus integration 7.6 = 54.1, which is 7.97% of 678.7 |
| Adjusted EBITDA bridge, trailing | 1,985.0 + 1,748.4 - 1,476.3 | 2,257.1, equal to the printed trailing figure |
| Cash conversion | Operating cash flow 950.1 / Adjusted EBITDA 1,748.4; Adjusted Free Cash Flow 484.9 / 1,748.4; prior 331.3 / 1,476.3 | 54.34%; 27.73%; prior 22.44% |
## Gaps
| Gap | Effect | Action |

| FY2025 audited statements, annual MD&A and contractual obligations table are not in the pack (the 40-F only lists them as exhibits, 40F page:5). Not supplied: FY2025 income statement, cash flow, full-year cash interest and year-end debt note | Trailing-twelve-month cash interest and full-year coverage are Not calculable; FY2025 appears only as year-end comparatives and management's 1,985.0 | Obtain the 40-F exhibits |

| No credit agreement or indentures | Reported covenant ratios, headroom, definitions, guarantors and restricted-group perimeter are Not supplied | Obtain the revolving credit agreement and indentures |
| USD principal not printed for most notes | Principal at original currency cannot be shown; CAD carrying values include foreign exchange translation | Use the indentures or annual debt note |

| No pension, factoring, litigation or consent-decree disclosure in interim statements | Absence in interim statements does not show absence in annual statements | Check annual exhibits |
## Next module

CP-1A should carry forward: the SECURE acquisition (completed September 1, 2026, total consideration 5,414.1, provisional accounting), the Term Loan B Facility, the Special Committee review with its November 9, 2026 deadline (after the cutoff, a future term), the Founder/CEO cash remuneration add-back and the related-party items; the missing annual information form means business description, ownership and control must be marked as not supplied. CP-2 should use the unadjusted leverage of 5.18x total and 5.05x net, management's 3.8x run-rate Net Leverage and the covenant levels together, state that covenant headroom is Not calculable, show liquidity as the 809.7 to 1,157.0 revolver range plus cash of 296.5, and label December 2025 figures as revised. CP-5 should check the quotes above against their pages, the 2025 comparative revision, and the capex basis difference (875.0 against 893.1).

Business, ownership and transaction fact pack for GFL Environmental Inc. (issuer id gfl), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, reporting currency CAD (context file). Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor. Perimeter: GFL Environmental Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries; amounts are CAD millions under IFRS unless stated. Every fact row carries one category: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation or Insufficient Information. No outside knowledge is used; labels such as "fourth largest" are management claims. No source dated after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used as fact. Figures repeated from the CP-1 handoff are repeated exactly. Governance is assessed at issuer level from documented actions only; no individual is assessed and no inference is drawn from sponsor identity. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| GFL is a scaled North American waste operator whose growth is mostly acquisition-led. The largest acquisition closed on September 1, 2026, and a take-private review is open, so structure and leverage may change. | Medium | No annual information form, so ownership, control rights, customer concentration and the terms of the acquisition and any bids are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Third quarter 2026 revenue growth of 27.2% was 18.7% from acquisitions and 7.4% organic, with volume slightly negative. | Pricing and acquisitions drive growth, so earnings depend on continued price realisation and integration. | High |

| SECURE added Western Canada processing and disposal assets and raised Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles from 1,942.0 to 6,902.2. | Business mix shifts toward energy-linked waste with new commodity-related commitments. | Medium |
| A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals, with updated proposals due November 9, 2026. | Ownership, financing and covenants could change; no terms are known. | Medium |

| Cash payments added back to Adjusted EBITDA include 74.2 of Founder and CEO remuneration, and share repurchases fell from 2,758.5 for nine months 2025 to 71.0 for nine months 2026. | Shareholder returns have slowed in 2026 while acquisition spending rose. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

GFL is a diversified solid waste and industrial waste processing business in Canada and the United States whose 2026 credit story is acquisition-driven. In the third quarter of 2026 acquisitions contributed 18.7% of the 27.2% revenue growth, organic growth was 7.4% of which price was 5.7% and volume was negative, so the operating model currently relies on price realisation and acquired scale rather than volume. The SECURE acquisition (completed September 1, 2026, total consideration approximately 5,414.1, funded with 4,334.8 of shares and 1,079.3 of cash) is the transaction that changes the credit: it raised Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangible assets from 1,942.0 to 6,902.2, added Western Canada industrial waste processing, disposal and recycling, and brought new crude oil transportation and storage commitments that did not exist at year-end 2025. The accounting is provisional, and the debt financing is documented in the CP-1 handoff rather than by transaction-level sources, so use of proceeds is partly inferred. There is no sponsor named in the sources, the controlling shareholder position is not described, and the board has formed a Special Committee to review unsolicited proposals to take the company private; the outcome is after the cutoff and no terms are supplied. Governance evidence is mixed: documented actions include a large 2025 share repurchase and a cash payment to the Founder and CEO in place of share-unit settlement, offset by an independent committee process. Business description, customer concentration, contract tenor and control rights are Insufficient Information because the annual information form is not in the pack.
### Company and operating model

| Growth sources, Q3 2026 | Acquisitions 18.7%, organic 7.4%, foreign exchange 1.1%, total 27.2%; organic is price 5.7%, surcharges 1.5%, volume (0.1)%, commodity price 0.3% | Documentary Fact | Q3PR page:13 | Volume was negative in Q3 2026 and (0.6)% for nine months 2026; growth rests on price |

| Cost structure, Q3 2026 | Cost of sales 1,728.7 and selling, general and administrative 277.2 against revenue 2,155.3 | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:1 | Cost of sales is 80.2% of revenue (Calculations); fuel and labour split not supplied |

| Closure and post-closure liabilities | 1,503.8 at Sep 30, 2026 against 1,170.5 at Dec 31, 2025, including 272.8 from acquisitions; 38.9 of legally restricted trust assets | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:11 | Long-dated landfill obligations rank outside debt; cash timing beyond the current portion of 68.7 is not supplied |

### Company profile
| Item | Value | Category | Locator | Limitation |

| Legal entity | `GFL Environmental Inc. (“GFL” or the “Company”) was formed on March 5, 2020 under the laws of the Province of Ontario.` | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:4 | Subsidiary structure and guarantor group are not supplied |

| Country and sector | Canada (context); sector Refuse Systems (context); registrant's standard industrial classification code 4953 | Documentary Fact | 40F page:1 | Context values are settings, not issuer evidence; the code is on the 40-F cover |
| Listing | Subordinate voting shares on the New York Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange, symbol GFL | Documentary Fact | 40F page:1 | None |

| Business | `GFL is in the business of providing non-hazardous solid waste management services and industrial waste processing and disposal.` | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:5 | Detailed description in the annual information form is absent |

| Scale and footprint | Management: `fourth largest diversified environmental services company in North America`; Canada and 19 U.S. states; more than 17,000 employees | Management Language | Q3PR page:4 | Ranking is a management claim and not verified |
| Offices | Registered office Vaughan, Ontario; executive headquarters Miami Beach, Florida | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:5 | None |

| Share capital, Sep 30, 2026 | Subordinate voting 424,203,668; multiple voting 11,812,964; preferred 13,063,727; total 449,080,359 | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:16 | Voting ratio of multiple voting shares and holders are not supplied |

| Preferred shares | Series A and Series B perpetual convertible preferred shares; amounts attributable to preferred shareholders of 34.0 for nine months 2026 | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:14 | Terms, holders and ranking not supplied; claims rank outside debt |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The principal transaction is the acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. A definitive agreement was entered on April 12, 2026 (`On April 12, 2026, GFL entered into a definitive agreement pursuant to which it has agreed to acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp.` (Q1FS page:15)), with consideration satisfied by a combination of subordinate voting shares and cash. Management said SECURE shareholders approved it in May (`SECURE shareholders approved the transaction in May` (Q2PR page:1), Management Language), and it closed on September 1, 2026 for total consideration of approximately 5,414.1, of which 4,334.8 was shares and 1,079.3 cash, with 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares issued in the nine months (Q3FS page:6 and page:16). SECURE is described as `an operator of waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling located in Western Canada and North Dakota` (Q3FS page:7). The purchase price allocation is provisional: goodwill recognized for SECURE is 4,968.1, property and equipment 1,616.9, other long-term liabilities 1,006.6 and closure obligations 271.8 (Q3FS page:6), and adjustments `may significantly impact the recognized values of intangible assets, goodwill, property and equipment and deferred income tax liabilities` (Q3FS page:7). SECURE net working capital includes cash of 73.4. No source identifies a sponsor. A SECURE nominee joins the board, which grows to nine directors (Q3PR page:2). The status is completed, with provisional accounting.

Other acquisitions: GFL acquired 13 businesses in nine months 2026 including SECURE (the note says each is individually immaterial except SECURE), 3 in Q1 and 10 for the six months, so 3 in Q3 including SECURE. Total net assets acquired in the nine months were 7,012.6 including SECURE, of which others 1,598.5, with 2,569.8 of cash paid net of cash acquired. This corrects the CP-1 handoff, which described the 13 as other businesses besides SECURE; the note's wording and the six-month count of 10 indicate the 13 includes SECURE. Management describes year-to-date completed acquisitions as generating approximately 2 billion of annualized revenue (Q3PR page:1, Management Language). Pro forma nine-month revenue as if all 2026 acquisitions had occurred on January 1, 2026 would have been 6,905.3 against 5,746.9 reported (Q3FS page:8).

New debt in 2026, as documented in the interim debt notes (use of proceeds is not stated in any source, so purpose is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows 6,795.9 issued and 3,823.9 repaid in nine months 2026): the 5.500% 2034 Notes appear first on the March 31, 2026 balance sheet at 1,393.9 (Q1FS page:8), the 5.625% 2031 Notes first on the June 30, 2026 balance sheet at 1,065.8 (Q2FS page:10) with a cross-currency swap on June 25, 2026, and the Term Loan B Facility was entered on August 28, 2026, maturing August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at 1,418.8, with a swap fixing 5.009%. Exact issue dates, USD principal amounts and guarantors of the notes and the Term Loan B Facility are Not supplied. The revolving credit agreement was amended and restated through September 1, 2026, with a maturity of April 29, 2030 (Q3FS page:12). Liquidity effect and leverage effect are in the CP-1 handoff: total debt 11,696.4 against 7,426.7 at year-end 2025, unadjusted total debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 5.18x and management Net Leverage of 3.8x.

Earlier history relevant to credit: effective March 1, 2025 GFL divested its Environmental Services line of business, retaining an option to repurchase the balance (`GFL has the option to repurchase the balance of the equity of GFL Environmental Services (the “Call Option”).` (Q3FS page:8)); the Call Option had a fair value of 95.0 at September 30, 2026 against 140.0 at year-end 2025. The nine-month 2025 cash flow shows divestiture proceeds of 5,817.1, long-term debt repayments of 4,294.0 and share repurchases of 2,758.5 (Q3FS page:4); the equity statement shows 40,327,898 shares repurchased and cancelled for 2,813.6 (Q3FS page:3). The relationship continues commercially: revenue from GFL Environmental Services of 29.1 for nine months 2026 and net payables of 13.7 (Q3FS page:19).

Events after the period: the Q3 statements contain no subsequent-events note. The Q3 release dated October 28, 2026 states that `we formed a Special Committee of independent directors to review unsolicited inbound proposals to take the Company private` (Q3PR page:1) with `a final deadline of November 9, 2026 to deliver their updated proposals` (Q3PR page:1). That date is after the 2026-11-05 cutoff and is a future term. The same release says there is no assurance a proposal will be received or negotiations will result in binding agreements (Q3PR page:6). The first disclosure was the July 29, 2026 release (`unsolicited preliminary expressions of interest from multiple parties to take the company private` (Q2PR page:2)). Bidders, price, financing and any change-of-control terms are Not supplied, so no effect on the debt documents can be assessed.
### Ownership, governance and behaviour

Each row is issuer-level and documented. Legal capacity (what documents permit) cannot be assessed because no credit documents are in the pack; willingness is what was done; feasibility is liquidity and leverage from the CP-1 handoff.
| Behaviour or fact | Evidence | Category | Mechanic and credit implication | Evidence quality |

| Share repurchases | 2,758.5 of repurchases in nine months 2025 against 71.0 in nine months 2026 (Q3FS page:4); a normal course issuer bid allows up to 27,396,513 shares until March 2, 2027 (Q3FS page:16) | Documentary Fact | Large 2025 buybacks coincided with divestiture proceeds of 5,817.1 (the sources do not say how proceeds were allocated); 2026 purchases slowed as acquisitions rose. The bid continues to permit cash returns while leverage is higher | High |
| Dividends | 24.5 paid in nine months 2026 against 23.5 in nine months 2025 (Q3FS page:4) | Documentary Fact | Small relative to cash flow; no debt-funded distribution is documented | High |

| Founder and CEO cash remuneration | `Consists of cash payment to the Founder and CEO, which payment had been previously satisfied through the issuance of restricted share units.` of 74.2 for nine months 2026 against 31.8 (Q3FS page:16) | Documentary Fact | A cash cost excluded from Adjusted EBITDA and added back to free cash flow, which lowers cash available for debt service relative to the reported measure | High |

| Related-party items | Lease payments to related parties of 11.8 for nine months 2026; GFL paid 33.5 in 2025 for the CEO relocation tax obligation, expected to be refunded and recognized as a receivable (Q3FS page:19) | Documentary Fact | Small amounts; leakage risk is low on the evidence, but related-party lease terms are not supplied | Medium |

| Collateral release on the 6.750% notes | `Collateral securing the 6.750% 2031 Secured Notes has been released pursuant to the terms of the indenture governing such notes.` (Q3FS page:12) | Documentary Fact | Released under the indenture's own terms, not through a non-pro-rata transaction; the trigger is not supplied, so it is neither adverse nor supportive | Medium |

| Process for the take-private review | Special Committee of independent directors (Q3PR page:1) | Documentary Fact | Formal process for conflicts; the CEO is also the founder, and holders' rights in a sale are not supplied | Medium |

| Overall behaviour category | Neutral or Mixed: documented actions combine shareholder returns and acquisition-funded growth with transparent reporting | Analyst Interpretation | Willingness to support creditors is neither shown nor contradicted; no sponsor behaviour exists to assess | Medium |
| Control rights of the multiple voting shares, holders and board composition | Not supplied | Insufficient Information | Control and change-of-control exposure cannot be assessed | Insufficient |
### Timeline

| September 1, 2026 | SECURE acquired; revolving credit agreement amended and restated | Documentary Fact | Q3FS page:7 |

### Credit translations
| Conclusion | Evidence | Risk mechanic | Credit implication | Counter-evidence and category |

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| GFL is a scaled waste operator whose leverage rose sharply with the SECURE acquisition. The credit view is cautious: unadjusted leverage is 5.18x while management's run-rate figure is 3.8x, so integration and the covenant definition decide the outcome. | Medium | The credit agreement, annual statements and take-private terms are not supplied, so covenant headroom and event risk cannot be sized. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt rose to CAD 11,696.4 million from CAD 7,426.7 million at year-end 2025. | Leverage is the weakest point; refinancing and deleveraging depend on SECURE earnings arriving. | High |
| Collection is 60.9% of gross revenue and Q3 2026 organic growth of 7.4% was price-led. | Recurring revenue supports debt service, but volume was slightly negative. | Medium |

| Revolver availability is derived at CAD 809.7 million to CAD 1,157.0 million plus cash of CAD 296.5 million. | Near-term liquidity looks adequate, and no named maturity falls before 2028. | Medium |
| A take-private review is open, with updated proposals due November 9, 2026. | Ownership, financing and covenants may change; nothing can be sized. | Medium |
### Credit view

GFL is a scaled, price-led North American waste operator whose credit has become more leveraged, and the fundamental view is cautious but not adverse. The strongest support is recurring collection revenue and a Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.5% with no named maturity until 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt is 5.18x trailing Adjusted EBITDA on an unadjusted basis against management's 3.8x run-rate figure, which relies on CAD 730.9 million of management adjustments. The outcome is decided by whether SECURE earnings and synergies arrive, how the revolver covenant defines its debt and EBITDA, and what the open take-private review brings.
### Key findings

Debt has stepped up faster than earnings, and the leverage reading depends on the definition. GFL carried CAD 11,696.4 million of debt before deferred costs at September 30, 2026, up from CAD 7,426.7 million at year-end 2025 [CP-1 financial table], while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is CAD 2,257.1 million and includes SECURE for only the month after its September 1, 2026 closing [CP-1 chart data: leverage]. Unadjusted, that is 5.18x total and 5.05x net; management's run-rate basis adds CAD 730.9 million to reach 3.8x [CP-1]. The revolver test is 5.00x for four quarters after a Material Acquisition and management states compliance, but the agreement's own definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable and the unadjusted figure should not be read as a breach [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]. This is Analyst Interpretation resting on Documentary Fact figures.

Operating performance is solid but growth is bought and priced rather than volume-led. In Q3 2026 revenue rose 27.2%, of which acquisitions were 18.7% and organic 7.4%, with price 5.7% and volume (0.1)% [CP-1A company and operating model]. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 678.7 million, up from CAD 535.1 million, at a 31.5% margin against 31.6% a year earlier, while the USA segment margin fell 2.3 points and Canada rose 2.1 points. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months 2026 against income of CAD 123.5 million, driven by CAD 482.9 million of interest and other finance costs and non-cash foreign exchange and fair-value charges, so earnings quality rests on the management measure [CP-1].

Cash flow covers interest on a management basis but with less room than the headline. Interest paid in cash was CAD 371.7 million for nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 1,748.4 million, a 4.70x ratio, and Q3 cash interest of CAD 172.5 million was 46.1% above CAD 118.1 million a year earlier [CP-1 chart data: interest cover; Calculations]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes CAD 172.1 million of cash costs (transaction, integration and Founder and CEO cash remuneration) for nine months 2026, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million is a management measure after add-backs; operating cash flow was CAD 950.1 million after a CAD 193.1 million working-capital outflow [CP-1].

Liquidity and the maturity profile are manageable near term. Cash is CAD 296.5 million and the derived revolver availability is CAD 809.7 million to CAD 1,157.0 million, depending on how letters of credit are allocated; the revolver matures on April 29, 2030 and the Term Loan B Facility on August 28, 2033 [CP-1 liquidity]. The named maturities cluster in 2028 to 2031, totalling CAD 7,621.4 million, or 65.2% of debt before deferred costs (Calculations), so refinancing capacity in those years will matter [CP-1 chart data: debt maturities].

Claims outside Note 7 debt add to the burden: lease obligations of CAD 705.0 million, closure and post-closure obligations of CAD 1,503.8 million, letters of credit of CAD 535.1 million, performance bonds of CAD 2,324.1 million, and new crude oil transportation commitments of CAD 561.4 million with onerous storage commitments of CAD 51.0 million that did not exist at year-end 2025 [CP-1 claims outside the debt figure; CP-1A company and operating model]. Pensions, factoring and litigation funding were not found in the interim sources.

Ownership and governance are unresolved rather than adverse. A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals, with updated proposals due on November 9, 2026, after the cutoff, and no terms are supplied [CP-1A transaction summary]. Documented actions are mixed: nine-month 2025 share repurchases of CAD 2,758.5 million against CAD 71.0 million in 2026, and a cash payment to the Founder and CEO of CAD 74.2 million in place of share-unit settlement [CP-1A ownership, governance and behaviour]. No sponsor, ratings or control-rights information is supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, recurring route-based revenue: collection is 60.9% of gross revenue for nine months 2026, which gives revenue visibility even though contract terms are not supplied (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact rows [CP-1A company and operating model]). Second, pricing power in the reported numbers: Q3 2026 price of 5.7% and surcharges of 1.5% drove organic growth of 7.4%, and the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.4% against 29.9% (Documentary Fact [CP-1A; CP-1]). Third, funding diversification and a staggered profile: a revolver to April 2030, a Term Loan B Facility to August 2033 and eight series of notes with maturities from 2028 to 2034, with no named instrument due before 2028 (Documentary Fact [CP-1 debt instruments]). Fourth, cash conversion improved on the management measure, with Adjusted Free Cash Flow of CAD 484.9 million against CAD 331.3 million (Management Language [CP-1]). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated by the issuer at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact, issuer assertion [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]). Sixth, an independent committee process governs the take-private review (Documentary Fact [CP-1A ownership, governance and behaviour]).

Weaknesses. First, leverage: debt before deferred costs rose by CAD 4,269.7 million in nine months and unadjusted leverage is 5.18x total and 5.05x net, both above the 5.00x covenant level although the covenant uses its own definitions, with the run-rate figure of 3.8x resting on CAD 730.9 million of management adjustments (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact figures [CP-1]). Second, acquisition dependence and integration risk: acquisitions were 18.7% of Q3 growth, SECURE accounting is provisional, and Canada segment goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles rose from CAD 1,942.0 million to CAD 6,902.2 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Third, soft volume and a falling USA margin: volume was (0.1)% in Q3 2026 and (0.6)% for nine months 2026, and the USA margin fell 2.3 points (Documentary Fact [CP-1A]). Fourth, earnings quality: CAD 172.1 million of cash costs are added back and the nine-month net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Fifth, a rising interest burden: Q3 cash interest of CAD 172.5 million against CAD 118.1 million a year earlier, while Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8% (Documentary Fact [CP-1]). Sixth, new energy-linked commitments: crude oil transportation commitments of CAD 561.4 million coincide with the SECURE closing but the sources do not tie them to it (Analyst Interpretation [CP-1A]). Seventh, unresolved ownership: the take-private review could change financing and covenants, and control rights are Insufficient Information (Management Language on the review; Insufficient Information on control [CP-1A]).

| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Cautious fundamental credit view: stable operations and adequate near-term liquidity, but leverage stepped up with SECURE and headroom against the revolver covenant cannot be measured | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and covenant figures; CP-1A transaction and operating model rows |

| Thesis | GFL's recurring, price-led waste revenue supports its debt service, but the credit depends on SECURE earnings and synergies bringing leverage from 5.18x unadjusted toward management's 3.8x | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same basis |
| Confidence limit | Below High because the CP-1A readiness judgment of CP-2 is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY | Documentary Fact | n/a | CP-1A consumer assessment |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Leverage and covenant headroom | Debt of CAD 11,696.4 million against trailing Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 2,257.1 million with one month of SECURE; the covenant defines its own terms | Headroom against the 5.00x test is unknown; a shortfall in run-rate delivery would reduce room and raise refinancing pressure | Material |

| Integration and provisional SECURE accounting | Provisional values for goodwill, intangibles and property can be restated; energy-linked commitments are new | Earnings and asset values supporting leverage could differ from the initial allocation | Material |
| Price and volume dependence | Organic growth is price-led with volume at (0.1)% | If price realisation slows, margin and cash flow growth weaken while acquisition debt stays | Material |
| Take-private event | Updated proposals due November 9, 2026, after the cutoff; terms unknown | Change of ownership or added debt could alter structure and covenants | Material |
| Refinancing in 2028 to 2031 | CAD 7,621.4 million of named maturities in four years | Market access determines refinancing cost and extension | Minor |

| Claims outside debt | Leases, closure obligations, letters of credit, performance bonds and commodity commitments | These call on cash outside the debt figure and are not captured by the leverage ratios | Minor |
| Earnings quality | Cash add-backs of CAD 172.1 million; management-defined free cash flow | Cash available for debt reduction is lower than the management measure suggests | Minor |
